Lets the President send weapons, equipment, services, and training from existing Defense Department stocks to a foreign country in an emergency or for listed purposes, without a new appropriation. Replacing what is drawn down takes separate appropriations, which is why large drawdowns are usually paired with supplemental funding.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 75 Stat. 437](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/75/437){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2318](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2318?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 506(a)(1): up to $100 million a year in defense articles, services, and training for an unforeseen emergency that cannot be met under the Arms Export Control Act or other law.
- Sec. 506(a)(2): up to $200 million a year, from any agency, for counternarcotics, disaster relief, antiterrorism, nonproliferation, refugee assistance, and cooperation with Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos on U.S. personnel missing from the Vietnam War.
- Each drawdown rests on a presidential determination reported to Congress.

## Why it matters

Drawdown is the fastest way to arm a partner because the equipment already exists. It carried most early U.S. military aid to Ukraine after February 2022, and its use there raised standing questions about the pace of replenishment, the effect on U.S. readiness, and how Congress tracks value drawn from stocks. Its contrast is [Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative](usai-2016.qmd), which buys new equipment instead.

## Current status

In force. The annual caps can be raised by statute, as supplemental appropriations acts for Ukraine did in 2022 through 2024. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Funding and administration

- **Account.** None for the articles, which come from existing stocks; replacement is funded later, replacement through Defense appropriations, often in supplementals in the [Defense appropriations (annual)](defense-approps-annual.qmd).
- **Run by.** The Defense Department, which executes drawdowns, with the State Department coordinating policy.
- **Committees.** Authorizing, House Foreign Affairs and Senate Foreign Relations; replacement funds, the House and Senate Defense appropriations subcommittees.
